x: The only other change was O'Hara passing Black and moving up on Dabbs, who was not sorry to see the finish on this occasion. Of the others Chris Keavey and Bob Glover ran well and it was good to see Bob enjoying his racing once again.
Charlie Smart (still going very strongly at the age of 55!), Gordon Biscoe, Don Maclean (one of his off days), George Piddington and Chris Keavey completed our two teams.
Highlights of this meeting were the 100 yards in which Cliff Brooks clocked 10.4 and the mile where Chris Keavey and Don Newell were given a rare chance to show their mettle.
On the second lap the 'A' team, through Peter Hilliar, moved up to 15th while Chris Keavey brought the 'B' team in 19th. It was on the third lap that it all began to happen.
Laurie O'Hara ran well to finish 5th in this long '5',Charlie Walker and Chris Keavey completing our scoring three. Phil King, Charlie Smart and Ron Langheim made up our much depleted team.

Joe Reilly was starting to make some impression after a slowish start and Howard Satchell, who was originally only reserve, had dispatched Chris Keavey etc. and for a few glorious miles had his sights trained on Ranjit Bhatia and John Dear.
Unfortunately, Trevor was the only "top man" present and we had to wait till 56th place for our 2nd scorer, Arthur Bruce. Chris Keavey and Peter Hilliar completed the 'A' team.

Charlie Dabbs turned in another of his fine performances to take 18th place while, with Mel Thorpe kept out of the race because of 'flu', a private battle ensued further down the field between Chris Keavey and Gordon Biscoe to decide who should complete the scoring three.

Ron Linstead illustrated his steady return to form with a useful 30:50 and, with a solid winter behind him, could well chop 2 minutes off that next year, The handicap went deservedly to Chris Keavey, a much improved runner who has had to work very hard to make his mark.

Having claimed this as a'personal best' he set off with Chris.Keavey to find liquid refreshments and celebrate. When the race did get under way, ideal conditions and a flat (although confusing) course decreed a fast pace and Gerry North, not at his best, found himself working to stay with the leader…
Eric Penny and Chris Keavey again continued to show an improvement, whilst Don Maclean found the course, the heat and achilles trouble a little too much for one afternoon.

Trevor Hart, ever willing to please and making his first return after injury, added to the shocks with an unexpected fine run while Chris Keavey continued the trend further down the field, with probably his best run of late.
John Bicourt, Chris Keavey and Gordon Biscoe also started but unfortunately the first two fell by the wayside during the race and Gordon was unhappy with his form despit finishing.
Don Maclean showed he is returning to fitness by beating drinking partner Chris Keavey and Gordon Biscoe, who was still looking rather flushed after his exertions during the afternoon.
Pat O'Connor showed a slight improvement on his loss of form of late but Chris Keavey and Bernard Merry would prefer to write this off as just not being their day.

Chris Keavey took second place, off 560 yards, while Guy Monnet raced through to third place, off 220. There was a good run from Alan Black, but the fastest moving man in the field was 17-year old Peter Carton, who clocked 9m. 31s. off 120.

Thanks must go to these, and also, especially, to Chris Keavey, who donned his kit to do the "B" 3,000m. steeplechase. Thanks go to to every competitor this summer, as I am sure they tried their hardest, and also to officials, notably Bob Taylor, who put in so much hard work and worry.
